title: tsconfig.json paths/baseUrl import resolution
description:
The JS/TS import resolver (src/js_imports.rs) handles relative imports and leaves bare specifiers unresolved. Real-world TS projects commonly use tsconfig.json `paths` and `baseUrl` to define path aliases (e.g. `@/components/Foo` → `src/components/Foo.tsx`). Without this, imports using path aliases stay unresolved — sutra_deps returns no edges for them, and DD constraints (forbidden_dep, boundary) can't see those dependencies.

Scope:
1. Parse `tsconfig.json` (and `jsconfig.json`) from workspace root, following `extends` chains
2. Extract `compilerOptions.baseUrl` and `compilerOptions.paths` mappings
3. In `resolve_js_imports`, after relative-import resolution fails, attempt path alias resolution: match the import specifier against `paths` patterns (glob-style with `*` wildcard), substitute, and resolve relative to `baseUrl`
4. Cache the parsed tsconfig per workspace (it doesn't change between imports)

Edge cases:
- `paths` with multiple candidates (first match wins, per TS behavior)
- `baseUrl` without `paths` (all bare specifiers resolve relative to baseUrl)
- Nested tsconfigs in monorepos (out of scope for v1 — use workspace root's tsconfig)
- `extends` pointing to node_modules presets (e.g. `@tsconfig/node18`) — best-effort, skip if unresolvable

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review: needs-attention (3 findings)

1. [high] JSONC tsconfigs silently ignored — serde_json::from_str fails on comments/trailing commas common in real tsconfig files. FIXED in 3cf8be5: added strip_jsonc() + warn on parse failure.

2. [medium] Path alias priority nondeterministic — HashMap iteration order. FIXED in 3cf8be5: switched to Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> preserving JSON key order.

3. [medium] Extended config paths resolved against wrong directory — inherited baseUrl/paths strings not normalized to workspace-relative. NOT FIXED: task explicitly scopes out subdirectory configs ("Nested tsconfigs in monorepos — out of scope for v1"). The extends chain is same-directory siblings in all supported cases."
